Frankfurt is a small city with a big history. Did you know the first ever German parliament was held here? 

This self guided audio tour is about finding your way around the city centre and enjoying fun facts and interesting sights, that you would never discover on your own. You'll start at Frankfurt's beautiful old opera house and walk right through the modern shopping heart to the Altstadt, discovering the stock market, Goethe's house, a peace garden, the new Old Town and much more along the way. I’ll explain why the old Hühnermarkt ( chicken market) was rebuilt and tell you how the town hall came to be called the Römer. 

You’ll see these landmarks along the way:

• The 19th century opera house and stock exchange
• The bull and bear statues
• Stunning replicated architecture of the old Hühnermarkt
• The Kleinmarkthalle (indoor market)
• The Eisenersteg and views of the River Main

- Sculptural features: The arch is adorned with reliefs and sculptures commemorating military achievements. The best-known work is the large group The Departure of the Volunteers (also known as La Marseillaise) by François Rude. Other reliefs and sculptures by artists such as Jean-Pierre Cortot and Antoine Étex decorate the exterior and interior faces.
- Inscriptions: The inner and outer faces bear the names of generals and battles from the era.
- Interior/exhibits: The base houses information about the monument’s history and context. The view from the top is a major draw.

- Photo spots: The Arc makes for dramatic photos, especially when approached from the Champs-Élysées or at night when it’s illuminated.
- Nearby attractions: The Champs-Élysées, the Grand Palais, the Tuileries and Louvre area, and the Eiffel Tower are all within easy reach if you’re doing a longer day of sightseeing.

- Best times: Early morning or later in the evening to avoid crowds; sunsets can offer especially nice light on the monument.
- Tickets/hours: Opening hours and ticketing can vary with seasons and renovations. Check the official site or local tourism pages for current hours and costs before you go.
- Getting there: If you’re using public transit, the Charles de Gaulle–Étoile station (lines 1, 2, 6) or nearby bus routes are convenient. The roundabout around the Arc is busy with traffic, so plan a few extra minutes for approach.

  - Style: Mughal architecture that blends Persian, Indian, and Islamic influences.
  - Main material: white Makrana marble, quarried in Rajasthan.
  - Inlay work: pietra dura (inlaid semi-precious stones like lapis lazuli, jasper, turquoise, and emerald) decorating the surfaces.
  - Structure: a symmetrical complex with a central tomb chamber, a large bulbous dome, and four slender minarets at the corners.
  - Gardens and water: the surrounding Charbagh (quadrilateral garden) is laid out with a long reflecting pool that mirrors the mausoleum, creating a striking visual effect.
  - Cenotaphs: the tombs of Mumtaz Mahal and Shah Jahan sit in the inner chamber behind ornamental screens; the actual graves lie in a lower chamber.

  - The main dome rises about 35 meters (roughly 115 feet), with four corner minarets each around 40 meters tall.
  - The exterior is covered with intricate calligraphy from the Quran and delicate floral inlays.

  - Opening hours: typically open from early morning to late afternoon/evening, with the best light at sunrise and sunset. Note that some days or times may be adjusted for maintenance or security checks.

  - Tickets: there are different prices for foreign and domestic visitors, and there may be separate charges for cameras. Check the latest official rates before you go.

  - What to wear and bring: comfortable shoes for walking, modest clothing (as with many historic sites in India), and a light jacket if it’s cool in the morning. Carry water and your photo ID.
  - Security: expect bag checks and metal detectors at the entrance.

- Nearby sights and a possible day plan
  - Agra Fort: a massive fortress complex with royal palaces and courtyards, a short distance from the Taj.
  - Itmad-ud-Daulah (the “Baby Taj”): another beautiful marble tomb along the Yamuna.
  - Mehtab Bagh: a garden across the river that offers a great sunset view of the Taj across the water.
  - Fatehpur Sikri: a well-preserved ancient capital about an hour or two away if you’re up for a day trip.

- Quick fun facts
  - The Taj Mahal is often described as “the jewel of Muslim art in India” and a pinnacle of Mughal architecture.
  - Its beauty lies not just in white marble but in the interplay of light, shadow, and reflection—especially striking at dawn and dusk.

data.description:
Munich is the world capital of beer, which Bavarians consider to be a food (in fact they call it liquid bread). Discover with us the history of this indispensable product of Munich gastronomy and how it traveled from homes to monasteries, from breweries to Biergartens.

In an exclusive tasting, you will enjoy and learn to distinguish the most representative types of beer in the city: Weiss, Helles, Dunkles and Pilsen. In addition, you will try the typical Bavarian bread, the Bretzel.

You will also learn what The Law of Purity (Reinheistgebot) consists of, how yeast was introduced after its discovery in the 19th century, how Oktoberfest and the Spring Festival were born, or what the six great Bavarian brands are...

And, finally, we will reveal the secrets of the most famous brewery in the world: Hofbräuhaus.

An essential tour for beer lovers and to discover a fundamental part of the culture and history of Bavaria.

Richly furnished with furniture, works of art and personal objects, they convey the splendor and lifestyle of the Habsburgs during their reign.

data.description:
Embark on this full-day Rio de Janeiro City Tour with a guide and visit Rio de Janeiro's top landmarks and highlights.
We visit to Corcovado Mountain and the Christ the Redeemer statue going through the Paineiras route. The 20-minute drive to the base of the statue takes you through the Tijuca Forest and gives you a preview of the landscapes ahead. The statue stands 710 meters tall and from this vantage point, you’ll have sweeping views of the city.
We also visit the Sugar Loaf. The cable car ride to the top of the mountain is done in 2 stages: begin at the boarding station to Urca Mountain (224 meters) and then from Urca Mountain to the top of Sugarloaf Mountain (395 meters).
Let’s also stop at the Metropolitan Cathedral, the Arcos da Lapa with the traditional Selarón Staircase, the Sambadrome and the Maracanã Stadium.
This tour includes tour guide, tickets to the Christ the Redeemer and the Sugarloaf, Buffet lunch and round-trip transportation.
